hints.content:
The basic function $\cos(x)$ has a maximum point at $(0,1)$ and intersects its midline at $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},0\right)$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

Let's transform $\pink{\cos(x)}$ to $\blue{5\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}x-\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)-2}$ step by step and see how the graph changes along the way.

options.alt: A trigonometric wave on a x y coordinate plane. The y-axis scales by one. The x-axis scales by one. The wave travels up to one on the y-axis at the point (zero, one) and down to negative one on the y-axis intersecting the midline at the point (pi over two, zero). The wave is at one on the y-axis at negative two pi, zero, and two pi. It is at negative one on the y-axis at negative three pi, negative pi, pi, and three pi.

hints.content:
The transformation from $\pink{\cos(x)}$ to $\green{\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}x\right)}$ is a horizontal shrink by a factor of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so the intersection point's horizontal distance from the origin is shrunk from $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\cdot\dfrac{2}{\pi}=1$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

The transformation from $\green{\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}x\right)}$ to $\red{5\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}x\right)}$ is a vertical stretch by a factor of $5$, so the maximum point's vertical distance from the origin is stretched from $1$ to $5$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 2]]

options.alt: Two waves on a x y coordinate plane. The y-axis scales by one. The x-axis scales by one. One wave is dotted while the other wave is solid. The waves both travel up to one on the y-axis and down to negative one on the y-axis. The dotted wave is at one on the y-axis at the point (zero, one), negative two pi, zero, and two pi. It intersects the midline at the point (pi over two, zero). It is at negative one on the y-axis at negative three pi, negative pi, pi, and three pi. The solid wave touches one on the y-axis at zero. It intersects the midline at (one, zero). It touches negative one on the y-axis at negative ten, negative six, negative two, two, six, and ten.

Two waves on a x y coordinate plane. The y-axis scales by one. The x-axis scales by one. One wave is dotted while the other wave is solid. The waves both travel up to one on the y-axis and down to negative one on the y-axis. The dotted wave touches one on the y-axis at zero. It intersects the midline at (one, zero). It touches negative one on the y-axis at negative ten, negative six, negative two, two, six, and ten. The solid wave touches five on the y-axis at zero on the point (zero, five). It intersects the midline at (one, zero). It touches negative five on the y-axis at negative ten, negative six, negative two, two, six, and ten.

hints.content: The transformation from $\red{5\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}x\right)}$ to $\blue{5\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}x-\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)-2}$, which is equivalent to $5\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}(x-3)\right)-2$, is a translation to the right by $3$ units and a translation downwards by $2$ units.

As a result of these transformations, the maximum point is now at $\left(3,3\right)$ and the intersection with the midline is at $(4,-2)$.

The resulting graph looks as follows:

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A trigonometric wave on a x y coordinate plane. The y-axis scales by one. The x-axis scales by one. The wave travels up to three on the y-axis at the point (three, three) and down to negative seven on the y-axis intersecting the midline at the point (negative two, four). The wave is at negative seven on the y-axis at negative seven, negative three, one, five, and nine.

*Note that one moveable point always defines an extremum point in the graph and the other point always defines a neighbouring intersection with the midline.*
